To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the trace anomaly is well described by a polynomial in T 4 over a broad temperature range, and that the crossover temperature is approximately 190 MeV.
the trace anomaly and energy density are determined to within 20% uncertainty at T = 140-700 MeV on Nτ =8 lattices with staggered quarks.
the QCD EoS is now known to within 20% uncertainty at T = 140-700 MeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the QCD EoS at high temperature.
the calculation of the QCD Equation-of-State (EoS) using numerical simulations of QCD on the lattice.
understanding the properties of QCD at finite temperatures and densities.

the QCD equation of state at zero chemical potential and finite temperature has been determined with high precision and is now known to a few per cent over the range of temperatures of relevance for heavy ion collisions.
the EoS is well determined and can be used to extract thermodynamic properties of the QGP.
lattice QCD is now in a position to provide reliable estimates of the thermodynamics of strongly interacting matter in the temperature range of 140 700 M eV.
